summary: Weekly POC sync to review quantization experiments (INT8 vs FP8), discuss quality impact on key eval sets, and align on next steps for benchmarks and customer-side validation. Redwood reported ~1.7-1.9x throughput gains with INT8 and 2.8-3.1x memory reduction on model checkpoints; FP8 showed slightly higher throughput but inconsistent numeric stability on the long-sequence test. Customer flagged a small quality regression on intent-classification set (~1.5-2% relative drop) under INT8; action items assigned to reproduce deterministically and run customer trace.

Numerical stability and edge cases (long-context, decoding anomalies)
Benchmark plan for Dedicated node and customer trace

transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: ok everyone thanks for joining, this is our weekly POC sync on quant. we got Maya, Ethan, Priya from OptiMetrics, hi all
[00:07] Maya Lopez: hey thanks, excited to see results
[00:10] Ravi Singh: quick agenda: results recap, quality diffs, perf numbers, next steps. i'll run through the INT8/FP8 numbers first
[00:20] Ravi Singh: so on our side we ran the INT8 profile on the v2-13b-ish model using Redwood optimize pipeline, we saw throughput increase about 1.7x to 1.9x depending on batch and seq len; latency p95 improved roughly 12-18% at 8 token bursts
[00:35] Ethan Zhang: can you clarify the test infra? was that hosted or dedicated?
[00:38] Ravi Singh: these were on a c5-like cc gpus emulated node, basically our baseline is a single A100 equivalent. these are run in hosted env to get more data. we also ran FP8 experiments — FP8 gave slightly higher throughput (2.1x) but we observed more variance and a few decode anomalies on long-context >2k tokens
[01:00] Priya Menon: when you say decode anomalies, like hallucinations or token repetition?
[01:04] Ravi Singh: more like token repeats and occasional truncation in the middle of a response, seems to be numerical stability under certain attention patterns
[01:12] Jamie Park: important to note these are early FP8 profiles; some of the kernel paths are experimental. INT8 is more stable but you may see small quality delta
[01:22] Maya Lopez: ok what about accuracy metrics on our intent classification set? we care about precision on few critical intents
[01:27] Ravi Singh: we ran your intent eval and reranking suite. INT8 had a 1.5-2% relative drop on the intent micro-F1 for the smallest intents; reranking NDCG dropped about 0.8% on the long-tail examples
[01:40] Maya Lopez: that's concerning if it affects production. do you have per-intent breakdown? sometimes aggregate hides big regressions on one class
[01:47] Ravi Singh: yes, we flagged two intents where the drop is larger (3.8% relative). we'll share the per-intent CSV in the logs. also note that when we add KL-based calibration and small bias correction the delta shrinks to ~0.6%
[02:04] Alex Rivera: is calibration an extra runtime cost?
[02:08] Ravi Singh: minimal — it's a small linear correction applied on logits before softmax, negligible latency but requires a small calibration step during rollout
[02:14] Ethan Zhang: curious about the memory savings numbers — you mentioned checkpoint reduction
[02:18] Ravi Singh: yes INT8 gave ~2.8x-3.1x reduction in model memory footprint on disk and about 2.4x memory reduction in KV cache while serving; FP8 was similar or a touch better on footprint but again more unstable on peak sequences
[02:35] Priya Menon: did you test end-to-end throughput with our batching pattern? we have a lot of short requests
[02:40] Ravi Singh: we ran both short-burst and steady-state traces. for short requests INT8 helps because cache hits are lighter; for steady large batches FP8 had slightly better GPU utilization but requires tuned kernels
[02:52] Maya Lopez: any differences in tokenization or post-processing that could explain the classification delta?
[02:56] Ravi Singh: minor token alignment differences due to quant rounding, but our post-processing is the same. sometimes the rounding affects subtoken logits which cascades in tight thresholds
[03:08] Jamie Park: (interrupts) also worth calling out that we saw one outlier run where INT8 had a 5% drop — that was without the calibration step and a different seed. reproducibility is critical here
[03:20] Priya Menon: can you reproduce with a fixed seed? we need deterministic results to assess production risk
[03:25] Ravi Singh: yes that's in the action items; i'll attach the deterministic seed and config. we'll rerun with deterministic sampler and drop-in calibration
[03:32] Ethan Zhang: what about compliance — does quantization change audit logs or explainability?
[03:37] Jamie Park: no change to audit logs; predictions still logged. we will provide notes on explainability and how calibration impacts logits — no change in provenance, only numbers differ slightly
[03:46] Maya Lopez: any security concerns with FP8 kernels? we've seen vendors require special flags for relaxed FP math
[03:50] Ravi Singh: it's more of a numerical precision tradeoff. FP8 kernels use hardware support or emulation; we document the flags and we can run in strict IEEE mode if you want but that erodes perf gains
[03:59] Alex Rivera: ok for decision making: if INT8 gives stable ~1.8x perf and small delta reducible to <1% with calibration, is that our recommended path?
[04:07] Jamie Park: from Redwood's ops POV INT8 is the recommended conservative rollout for now. FP8 is interesting for future but needs more validation. we recommend pilot on INT8 with rollback plan
[04:16] Priya Menon: agreed. what's the planned timeline for the dedicated node benchmark?
[04:20] Ravi Singh: we propose next week, we'll schedule a 2-hour bench on a Dedicated node equivalent (p3/p4 configs) — we'll include end-to-end trace and compare hosted vs dedicated perf
[04:33] Maya Lopez: please include a canary config and the calibration model in that benchmark
[04:36] Jamie Park: yes will do. action items: we'll upload the full logs, the per-intent CSV and the quant scripts. also we'll add a notes doc about the calibration step and expected perf tradeoffs
[04:48] Ethan Zhang: sounds good. also can you include a short runbook for rollback if we see >2% production regressions?
[04:54] Ravi Singh: absolutely, we'll draft a rollback playbook (toggle profile, revert to fp16, re-deploy weights)
[05:02] Jamie Park: quick clarification, are you planning to run the customer-side trace with the same dataset we used for eval or a production sample?
[05:08] Priya Menon: we'll do a 1-hour production trace sample to surface real patterns, then share results
[05:13] Maya Lopez: ok last question on cost: what's the expected unit cost change if we move to INT8 on Dedicated?
[05:18] Jamie Park: rough estimate is 25-35% lower per-token cost due to memory and batching improvements; precise numbers depend on utilization and residual cache hit rates
[05:27] Alex Rivera: great, thanks everyone. recap of next steps?
[05:30] Jamie Park: recap: Redwood to share raw eval logs, per-intent CSV, quant scripts, calibration notes by 2025-04-03; Ravi to include deterministic seed; OptiMetrics to run 1-hour prod trace with INT8 profile and report regressions by 2025-04-07; schedule Dedicated benchmark for week of 2025-04-07 (propose 2025-04-08). we'll sync again same time next week
[05:55] (end of recording)
